Q: How to get the timestamps of lyrics in songs? A:

If you need a high level of precision, you'll be deeply disappointed by LRCLib and Lyricsify because they provide only phrase-level timestamps, i.e a timestamp for each group of words. It's better than nothing and maybe it's enough for your use case.

I publish my lyrics files in word-by-word (and occasionally syllable-aware) level of precision, I only have a few files right now, but maybe it can be helpful for you: https://sourceforge.net/p/librekaraoke/code/ci/master/tree/src/main/resources/captions/

You can use Python-ass to parse the ASS files in Python.

Q: How to calculate relative volume (RVOL) efficiently in Postgres A:

Execution Time: 18167.869 ms is expected for this shape because the query is calculating two ordered window aggregates for all 16672172 rows. An index can reduce some sorting, but each request still recomputes every historical cumulative value and every historical average.

For a response-time query, store the intermediate result you reuse: cumulative volume per symbol_id, day, and minute-of-day. Then the RVOL query reads that summary instead of running the nested windows over core_price each time.

Assuming timestamp is Unix seconds and UTC day/minute buckets are acceptable:

CREATE TABLE core_price_day_minute (
    symbol_id bigint NOT NULL,
    day_no int NOT NULL,
    minute_of_day int NOT NULL,
    cumulative_volume double precision NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (symbol_id, day_no, minute_of_day)
);

CREATE INDEX core_price_day_minute_rvol_idx
ON core_price_day_minute (symbol_id, minute_of_day, day_no)
INCLUDE (cumulative_volume);

Refresh only the day that is still changing:

WITH todays AS (
    SELECT
        symbol_id,
        ("timestamp" / 86400)::int AS day_no,
        (("timestamp" % 86400) / 60)::int AS minute_of_day,
        sum(volume) OVER (
            PARTITION BY symbol_id, ("timestamp" / 86400)
            ORDER BY "timestamp"
        ) AS cumulative_volume
    FROM core_price
    WHERE "timestamp" >= :today_start
      AND "timestamp" <  :tomorrow_start
)
INSERT INTO core_price_day_minute AS d
    (symbol_id, day_no, minute_of_day, cumulative_volume)
SELECT symbol_id, day_no, minute_of_day, cumulative_volume
FROM todays
ON CONFLICT (symbol_id, day_no, minute_of_day)
DO UPDATE SET cumulative_volume = EXCLUDED.cumulative_volume;

Then RVOL is a grouped lookup against prior days:

SELECT
    c.symbol_id,
    c.minute_of_day,
    c.cumulative_volume / avg(h.cumulative_volume) AS relative_volume
FROM core_price_day_minute c
JOIN core_price_day_minute h
  ON h.symbol_id = c.symbol_id
 AND h.minute_of_day = c.minute_of_day
 AND h.day_no < c.day_no
WHERE c.day_no = :today_day_no
GROUP BY c.symbol_id, c.minute_of_day, c.cumulative_volume;

A plain PostgreSQL materialized view is a poor fit for refreshing this whole result every minute, because REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW completely replaces the contents of the materialized view. Use a table like the above when only the latest day changes; use a materialized view only for a batch result that can be rebuilt on that schedule.

Q: Selenium Test opens the Chrome window in headless mode A:

Since Selenium v4.11.0, all the selenium4 bindings includes Selenium Manager which is a command-line tool implemented in Rust that provides automated driver and browser management for Selenium. Selenium bindings use this tool by default so you do not need to download it of use webdrivermanager to download any binaries or add anything to your code or do anything else to use it.

As you are using the maven dependency of Selenium v4.35.0, the in-built Selenium Manager will automatically take care of discovering, downloading, and cacheing the drivers required by Selenium when these drivers are unavailable.

So you can safely remove the WebDriverManager dependency.

Solution

The solution will be to downgrade google-chrome to previous version i.e. v149.x

Q: Problem with dynamic submenus: can't achieve a static reference from one sheet to another A:

I think the use case you describe should work fine if you use a script to create the dependent dropdowns using the Dropdowns (from a list) option instead of using cross-sheet references in with the Dropdowns (from a range).

See my dependentDropdowns_ script for one example.
